authoredFrom: The second shape the pass-2 corpus probe found: duckdb/src/include/duckdb/storage/serialization/*.json are serialisation schemas for C++ classes. `{ "class": "NotNullConstraint", "base": "Constraint", "constructor": ["index"] }` — `class` DECLARES the type, `base` names its superclass, and every superclass named is declared in the same file. Measured corpus-wide: 21 documents carry a `class` string, all duckdb. The two forbids that matter are the ones a shape-matching probe would have got wrong. (1) A MEMBER DESCRIPTOR: duckdb writes `{ "id": 200, "name": "info", "type": "AlterInfo*", "base": "ParseInfo" }` for a FIELD whose C++ class derives from ParseInfo — 16 such statements corpus-wide, and 13 of them name a type the document does not declare. An object with no `class` marker is not a type declaration, and the rule says so structurally rather than by a name list. (2) A reference to a type this document never declares (`Dangling` -> `ParseInfo`) produces NO edge, because an edge to a symbol the file does not contain is the fabrication the ontology workstream calls the most expensive mistake available. The `constructor` array is present deliberately and produces nothing: a constructor DECLARATION is the opposite of a construction, which is why `instantiates` stays ruled on evidence rather than on a grammar inventory.
